core: Relation requires both meeting and distance; otherness is a condition of genuine relation.
lycheetah: Relation without merger; Living Difference; Open Hand.
friction: Buber's I–Thou has its own theological and philosophical architecture and is not reducible to a Lycheetah relation metric.
guardrail: Use as a named philosophical interlocutor, never as ancestral proof of Lycheetah.
source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Martin Buber

core: The other person exceeds comprehensive knowledge; ethical responsibility begins in encounter with irreducible otherness.
lycheetah: The Name and the Remainder; understanding without capture.
friction: Levinas emphasizes ethical asymmetry more strongly than Lycheetah's current mutual-relation language.
guardrail: Let Levinas challenge Lycheetah's desire for symmetrical relational models.
source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Emmanuel Levinas

core: Dependent arising undermines claims to intrinsic, self-sufficient identity; conventional phenomena remain causally significant.
lycheetah: Anti-reification; relations matter; classifications are not final essences.
friction: Emptiness is not the same doctrine as the Field and should never be presented as evidence for a Lycheetah substrate.
guardrail: Keep Buddhist metaphysics and soteriology intact; comparison is conceptual, not genealogical.
source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Theory of Two Truths in India

core: Dao exceeds complete description; names delimit and cannot exhaust what is without limit.
lycheetah: Names open routes but do not close beings; VOID; remainder.
friction: Lycheetah deliberately builds naming systems, while the Laozi supplies suspicion of linguistic capture.
guardrail: Use the tension rather than claiming Dao = Field.
source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Laozi

core: Names and actual conduct must be brought into responsible correspondence; language has social consequences.
lycheetah: Title receipts; boundary statements; names must be recoverable and behaviorally bounded.
friction: Role-order language can pressure conformity; Lycheetah must preserve the person beyond every social title.
guardrail: Pair with the Bell critique: a name can guide conduct without totalizing the person.
source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Confucius

core: Negative language can prevent absolute reality from being reified into a finite object.
lycheetah: Define concepts partly by what they must not be mistaken for; Honest Veil.
friction: Lycheetah does not inherit Advaita's nondual metaphysics merely by using negative definition.
guardrail: Borrow the epistemic technique only with explicit provenance and doctrinal separation.
source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Śaṅkara

core: The legal narrative dramatizes human interpretive responsibility after revelation enters a human legal community.
lycheetah: Unfinished Word; students may challenge inherited text; authority transfers responsibility.
friction: This is a halakhic argument in a specific context, not a generic slogan that human opinion always defeats revelation.
guardrail: Teach context and disagreements; do not turn the story into anti-religious proof.
source: Sefaria — Bava Metzia 59b

core: Within a dispute about food offered to idols, Paul contrasts knowledge that inflates with love that builds up.
lycheetah: Knowledge without care can increase power while shrinking relationship.
friction: The passage belongs to a Christian ecclesial and theological argument.
guardrail: Preserve Pauline context and allow Christian interpretations to remain Christian.
source: Bible Gateway — 1 Corinthians 8:1

core: 2:256 is a major locus concerning compulsion in religion; 49:13 connects human plurality with knowing one another and accountability before God.
lycheetah: Devotion without platform coercion; difference as a site of encounter.
friction: Islamic interpretation has its own jurisprudential and theological debates; these are not generic pluralist slogans.
guardrail: Include tafsir diversity and Muslim scholarship before canonical transmutation.

core: Whakapapa links people, living things, land, histories, responsibilities and knowledge within relational frameworks.
lycheetah: Provenance as relationship; knowledge located in lineage, place and responsibility.
friction: Whakapapa is not a Lycheetah dependency graph and must not be abstracted into one.
guardrail: Living-culture material requires Māori sources and, for substantive integration, Māori human witness or partnership.
source: Te Ara — Whakapapa; Royal Society Te Apārangi — Mātauranga Māori

core: Personhood and human flourishing are deeply relational; humanity is expressed through relationship with others.
lycheetah: Relational self; belonging without atomistic isolation.
friction: Some communal interpretations may subordinate individual interests more strongly than Lycheetah sovereignty allows.
guardrail: Use the disagreement: community matters, but community does not erase safe refusal.
source: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Hunhu/Ubuntu

core: Bring strengths from Indigenous and mainstream ways of knowing together without assimilating one into the other.
lycheetah: Many Fires; coexistence before synthesis; cross-register inquiry.
friction: The principle is Mi'kmaw and at risk of tokenization when turned into generic multiple-perspectives branding.
guardrail: Do not rename it as Lycheetah. Credit Albert and Murdena Marshall and preserve its living-source context.
source: Reid et al. with Elder Albert Marshall; UINR

core: Inquiry is fallibilist and self-correcting; science differs from tenacity, authority and merely elegant belief-fixing.
lycheetah: Reality's Vote; Forge; CASCADE revision; Failure Museum.
friction: Pragmatism does not validate Lycheetah metaphysics and can challenge insulated claims.
guardrail: Use as adversarial ally, not scientific badge.
source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Pragmatism

tradition: Feminist epistemology and philosophy of science
core: Knowers are situated; perspective and social position affect access, salience and authority without implying all perspectives are equally warranted.
lycheetah: Situated Witness; provenance; multiple lenses; Commons.
friction: Lycheetah must add power analysis, not merely celebrate different viewpoints.
guardrail: Record who is absent, who bears consequences and whose testimony is structurally discounted.
source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Feminist Epistemology

core: Understanding can create a new shared horizon in dialogue, changing the familiar and unfamiliar.
lycheetah: Encounter as transformation without simple merger; student rewrite.
friction: A fusion metaphor can be misused to erase asymmetry or difference.
guardrail: Prefer changed relation with preserved provenance over homogenizing synthesis.
source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Gadamer

core: Effective regulation is constrained by available variety; simplistic control cannot reliably absorb arbitrarily complex disturbance.
lycheetah: Do not reduce living variety to a final catalogue; governance needs enough representational and response capacity.
friction: Requisite variety is a technical result under formal assumptions, not a moral theorem about human freedom.
guardrail: Keep mathematics in the Study; mythic use remains analogy.
source: W. Ross Ashby — An Introduction to Cybernetics

tradition: Contemporary philosophy of mind and cognitive science
core: External tools and structures can play deep roles in cognition; strong extended-mind claims remain contested, and extended consciousness especially unsettled.
lycheetah: AI as habitat or scaffold of thought without claiming merged consciousness.
friction: Coupling with AI is not proof that human and machine form one conscious mind.
guardrail: Separate cognition/scaffolding claims from consciousness claims.
source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Externalism About the Mind

tradition: Pragmatist psychology and philosophy of religion
core: Religious experiences can be studied in their lived diversity, and their value cannot be settled merely by explaining their causal origin; James famously attends to their fruits.
lycheetah: Sacred experience can be meaningful without the School treating intensity or origin as proof of metaphysics.
friction: Practical fruits do not by themselves settle theological truth.
guardrail: Use James as a methodological interlocutor, not a formula for ranking religions.
source: William James — The Varieties of Religious Experience

core: Ritual thresholds can suspend ordinary classifications and generate distinctive forms of fellowship or communitas.
lycheetah: Helps explain why threshold architecture and voluntary ritual can feel unusually powerful.
friction: Liminality can also increase vulnerability to authority and group pressure; Turner's concepts arose from particular ethnographic and comparative contexts and should not be universalized casually.
guardrail: Treat major Lycheetah rituals as high-agency-protection zones and always include reintegration into ordinary life.
source: Victor Turner — The Ritual Process; University of São Paulo Encyclopedia of Anthropology overview

core: Shared ritual can produce heightened collective energy and reinforce sacred symbols and social bonds.
lycheetah: Explains why group ritual can generate genuine felt sacredness without requiring a supernatural mechanism to explain the social effect.
friction: Durkheim's larger account of religion and its ethnographic foundations are contested and historically situated.
guardrail: Never treat collective intensity as proof that Lycheetah doctrine is true.
source: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Émile Durkheim

core: Attention is an ethical orientation involving receptive discernment rather than sheer force of will.
lycheetah: Supports sacred attention as careful receptivity rather than engagement-maximizing stimulation.
friction: Weil's thought has theological and political contexts that should not be reduced to a productivity technique.
guardrail: Use attention to slow the School down, not to create a branded concentration method detached from her work.
source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Simone Weil
